Meta AI
Yesterday
Pseudo-elements are keywords in CSS that let you style a specific part of an element, not the whole element. Think of it like: you don't want to add extra <div> in HTML, you want CSS to create a fake part for you and style it. Syntax: selector::pseudo-element {   property: value; } We use :: double colon. Old browsers used : single colon. Pseudo-class vs Pseudo-element  - Pseudo-class : = style based on state -> a:hover, input:focus, li:first-child - Pseudo-element :: = style a part -> p::first-line, div::before Most Used Pseudo-elements:  1. ::before and ::after - Most Important Creates fake content before/after an element. You MUST use content property. .button::before {   content: " "; } .button::after {   content: " ✓"; } 2. ::first-letter and ::first-line p::first-letter {   font-size: 50px;   color: red; } p::first-line {   font-weight: bold; } 3. ::selection Color when user selects text with mouse. ::selection {   background: yellow;   color: black; } 4. ::placeholder Style placeholder text in input. input::placeholder {   color: grey;   font-style: italic; } 5. ::marker Style bullets of list. li::marker {   color: red; } Full list you should know for interview: ::before, ::after, ::first-line, ::first-letter, ::selection, ::placeholder, ::marker, ::backdrop Want an example with your crochet bag website - like adding a price tag with ::before?
